answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with unit-capacity trust graphs. Each identity is a vertex in a vouching network where peers hold a small edge budget, and verifiers admit nodes via bounded max-flow from trusted anchors. Because narrow cuts cap throughput, each fake node costs scarce social capital to earn a signed honest endorsement, stemming a tide of bots. Yet links are never fixed in marble, so bribed insiders can still bridge honest regions to Sybil clusters.
